name: MeetGeek
summary: Meeting recorder and note-taker: transcription, summaries and searchable meeting history.
best_for: people who run many external meetings and need a searchable record — the summaries earn their keep when you cannot remember which of four calls a detail came from
skip_if: your meetings are internal and few, because the note-taking in your existing conferencing tool covers that; also skip Pro if you record daily, since twenty hours will not last
honest_knock: The meter is transcription hours and Pro gives you twenty a month, which is about an hour a working day. That sounds generous until you count the meetings you would actually record — a sales rep on four calls a day passes it in the first week, and the overage is $0.50 an hour. Unlimited transcription is the real reason to be on Business at $17, so treat Pro as a plan for occasional recording rather than a cheaper version of the same thing. Worth checking before you buy: consent. A recorder that joins every meeting changes what people say in them, and that is a policy decision rather than a pricing one.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-09-19 on meetgeek.ai/pricing; amounts unchanged since 2026-09-04) The page loads on annual billing, so the figures it shows first are the annual ones; both terms are given here. Basic is free with 3 hours of transcription a month. Pro $9.99 per user per month billed annually, $15.99 billed monthly, with 20 hours of transcription. Business $17 per user per month billed annually, $27 billed monthly, with unlimited transcription and team multi-meeting analytics. Enterprise is quote-only: SSO, SCIM, org-wide settings, on-premise storage, custom retention, custom voice agents and a dedicated account manager. Extra transcription hours are $0.50 each. Downloads and exports and admin user management start on Pro, not Business; API and MCP access are listed on the free Basic plan. A 14-day free trial runs on Pro. Two limits sit beside the hours and neither is in the plan blurb. A separate cap ends the individual meeting: two hours on Basic and Pro, three on Business, four on Enterprise. And your recordings expire on a schedule — transcripts are kept three months on Basic, a year on Pro and indefinitely above that, audio one month, six months and twelve, with video stored only from Business. On the same page, the annual badge claims up to 40% off, the actual step from monthly to annual is about 37% on both paid tiers, and a line under the heading offers 30% off for startups, non-profits and education on request. Data can be stored in the EU or the US on every plan, the page claims SOC 2, GDPR and HIPAA compliance and states that customer data is not used to train external models, but recording-consent notifications with approval tracking start on Business.
